title: Resolve five source-bound MediaDive form and alias holds from the fresh chemical queue
body:
# Bounded MediaDive source/form holds

Five targeted cases remain on hold; no further alias additions or mapping approvals are proposed. The sodium acetate1315 pilot is documented separately.

| Source | Exact raw name | Decision | Evidence and next step |
|---|---|---|---|
| mediadive.ingredient:331 | Tris(hydroxymethyl)methylamine | UPSTREAM_LABEL_NORMALIZATION_AND_EXISTING_OWNER_REVIEW | The admitted raw name Tris(hydroxymethyl)methylamine already occurs as an accepted EXACT_SYNONYM on Tris_Base; the transformed label removes parentheses. MediaDive identifies CHEBI9754/CAS77-86-1. That supports retaining the exact raw source spelling, not adding the damaged transformed form or approving this owner's whole row. The owner also carries Tris hydrochloride, Tris HCl, Tris buffer1M and nitrilotriacetic acid trisodium salt as accepted aliases: their salt/preparation/substance scopes require separate review before any full-payload approval. Preserve source-to-transformed provenance and the current native release hold. Review the existing Tris alias payload as a separate bounded curation; do not promote an entire row from this one raw-label agreement. [Source](https://mediadive.dsmz.de/download/ingredient/331/json). |
| mediadive.ingredient:1512 | Calcium D-(+)-pantothenate | UPSTREAM_LABEL_NORMALIZATION_AND_STEREOCHEMISTRY_HOLD | The raw Calcium D-(+)-pantothenate spelling already exists as accepted EXACT on Calcium_Pantothenate; the transformed spelling drops parentheses. MediaDive gives CAS137-08-6. The current owner mixes D and DL aliases and also carries unrelated-looking vanillylamide aliases recovered from SSSOM. This bounded source spelling comparison does not settle all those alias identities or permit a complete-row release. Keep the raw spelling and source CAS witness. Audit D versus DL and unrelated alias provenance before considering this owner's row; do not turn punctuation normalization into identity approval. [Source](https://mediadive.dsmz.de/download/ingredient/1512/json). |
| mediadive.ingredient:1930 | Nitrilotriacetic acid trisodium salt monohydrate | DISTINCT_HYDRATE_REQUIRES_SEPARATE_IDENTITY_REVIEW | MediaDive explicitly names nitrilotriacetic acid trisodium salt monohydrate and CAS18662-53-8. The nearby maintained trisodium nitrilotriacetate owner is CHEBI132766/CAS5064-31-3 with anhydrous structure. Section3 forbids treating the supplied hydrate as an exact alias of that different form; source hydration must remain explicit. Keep unresolved in this batch. A future exact-form review must resolve a hydrate-specific ontology identity locally or establish the documented CAS/local identity plus asymmetric parent. Do not guess hydration or import the source formula uncritically. [Source](https://mediadive.dsmz.de/download/ingredient/1930/json). |
| mediadive.ingredient:2160 | Na2SiO3 x 5 H2O | REJECTED_HYDRATE_ALIAS_AND_STOCK_CONTEXT_HOLD | MediaDive2160 names Na2SiO3 x5H2O and CAS10213-79-3. Its admitted raw occurrence says21.2g/l stock solution,1ml. The exact pentahydrate label is REJECTED_LABEL on Na-silicate; neither that generic/anhydrous scope nor the separate nonahydrate is the exact supplied hydrate. The source solution attribute also must survive. Preserve the rejected label and preparation context. Review the pentahydrate substance and the named stock separately if later curation is authorized; do not resurrect this alias on a different hydrate or generic owner. [Source](https://mediadive.dsmz.de/download/ingredient/2160/json). |
| mediadive.ingredient:776 | Maltose x H2O | CONTRADICTORY_SOURCE_HYDRATION_HOLD | The source label Maltose xH2O names a hydrate, but live MediaDive metadata gives anhydrous CAS69-79-4, CHEBI17306 and formulaC12H22O11. The exact label is already REJECTED_LABEL on Maltose. The general Maltose Hydrate local owner does not establish water number/anomer; the separate D-Maltose Monohydrate NCITC80300/CAS6363-53-7 owner cannot be selected from this conflicting source label alone. Retain the unresolved source label and its contradictory metadata; obtain original recipe/product evidence to decide hydrate and stereochemistry. No alias addition to anhydrous maltose and no automatic choice of the known monohydrate owner. [Source](https://mediadive.dsmz.de/download/ingredient/776/json). |

All current owner bytes, source captures/hashes, raw records and exact existing native dispositions are retained in `targeted-mediadive-holds-v1.json`. These are bounded triage conclusions, not whole-record or release approvals.

Historical #251 and broader open #811/#868 remain distinct from these exact new source observations. No issue is closed or claimed solved by this report.

Follow-up from #1149. Preserve all current WITHHOLD and REJECTED_LABEL decisions. This is a source-bound follow-up to the broader #718/#811/#868 queues, not authorization to map all five rows. Options are: verify exact supplied form/product from original recipe evidence and curate the correct separate owner; or preserve source-scoped unresolved status. Recommendation: keep the five holds until those specific identity checks are complete. No hydration, stereochemistry, or mixture inference from normalized names.

title: Typed companion successors reject the retained owned-name suppression history
body:
The three older typed companion-refresh paths reject the current canonical policy history before they can inspect a successor update. At MIM `0dac278466699129a083343a921c2e0ca18a9ab4`, `mappings/ingredient_mappings.sssom.tsv.manifest.json` legitimately contains `owned_name_suppression_updates` from the completed deferred-alias publication. `_verify_policy_projection` in `src/mediaingredientmech/ingredient_bundle_refresh.py` admits only the form, registry-correction and stock-CAS update keys. Its strict shape check therefore raises `Form projection: unknown manifest shape` for the actual current manifest in all three contexts.

This is a fail-closed successor compatibility defect, not a failure of the current release: the current native reviewed SSSOM export and replay both pass. It matters when a later authorized correction needs an explicit typed manifest successor. Removing the owned-name history or bypassing the verifier would lose provenance and is not an acceptable remedy.

Verified source pins:

- Shared verifier SHA256: `cd85ce90c88bb69b05d618492af6bdc7d27adfa12ca1a5c753bb223207ff4f32`.
- Current manifest SHA256: `6b6fe48246bd43dd70499e82f508a7b7ea0fcd121bccafafa0217aae84a17778`.
- Independent private probe: `.temp/kgm-unmapped-20261107/reviewer/probe_typed_history_v1.py` and `typed-history-proof-v1.json`.

The probe calls each native verifier with the exact current manifest and records the shape refusal. As a diagnostic control only, removing that one key in an in-memory copy reaches the later append-only guard instead. It changes no maintained file and does not claim that an incomplete synthetic successor should pass.

Acceptance requires preserving the existing owned-name history byte-for-byte as an immutable unrelated history for these typed successors, retaining each context's existing narrow scientific/receipt contract, and regression tests that reject omitted, altered or reordered retained history. A true alias-addition successor requires its own bounded contract; it must not masquerade as the existing `hydrate_parent_predicate` form transition. No owner merge, scientific approval, gate weakening or broader scope is authorized by this issue.

title: Na2so3_X_5_H2o (sodium sulfite hydrate) has the anhydrous CHEBI:86477 as its exact identity
body:
Found in the review of PR #881.

**The problem:** `data/ingredients/mapped/Na2so3_X_5_H2o.yaml` (a sodium sulfite hydrate) has identifier and ontology mapping `CHEBI:86477`, sodium sulfite (anhydrous), at `SYNONYM_MATCH`, with an SSSOM `skos:exactMatch`.

**Why it's wrong:** `MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md` §3 forbids mapping a hydrate to its anhydrous parent as an exact identity.

**Consequence:** because `Na2so3` carries the same id, PR #881's move of the "anhydrous sodium sulfite" names from `Na2so3_X_5_H2o` to `Na2so3` changes nothing for CultureMech or the KG.

**Existing tracking:** the only trace is the `HYDRATE_FAMILY_UNREVIEWED` row in `mappings/duplicate_identifier_baseline.tsv`. #321 is closed, and I found no open issue for this record.

**Fix:** follow the §3 decision procedure.
- If ChEBI has a term for this hydrate, ground to it.
- Otherwise, preserve a distinct `cas:` or `kgmicrobe.compound:` identity with a CLOSE_MATCH parent of CHEBI:86477.

Then update the SSSOM rows, the duplicate baseline and a mapping-change receipt.



## Update 2026-10-14 (second review of #881)

- **Correction to the suggested fix above:** where no ChEBI term exists, §3 step 2 needs three rows (see #897 for why `closeMatch` is wrong):
  - the `cas:` or `kgmicrobe.compound:` identity;
  - a `skos:broadMatch` (NARROW_MATCH) to CHEBI:86477;
  - the Rule B1 registry row.
- **More of the same defect:** `MIM:Na2so3`'s SSSOM `other` carries `Na2SO3 x 5 H2O`.
  - It is not a YAML synonym of `Na2so3`, so it came in from kg-microbe labels.
  - It is baselined under Rule K.
  - It should leave when this record is split.

title: 12 MAPPED labels resolve to an identity with a different hydrate; the MgSO4·H2O record sits on the heptahydrate
body:
Found from CultureBotAI/CultureMech#597, using CultureMech's `label_hydrate_count` (CultureMech#591) over the label index at `6643131b`. These are **MAPPED** rows, MIM's curated answers. CultureMech honours MAPPED answers and does not override them, so they can only be fixed here.

Each row's label states an explicit hydrate count. Its identifier's count comes from the index itself: the identity's `ontology_label` rows when they state one, otherwise its MAPPED preferred terms. Recipe rows are occurrences in CultureMech `41d4d39`.

## A. Wrong identity: label hydrate ≠ identity hydrate (12 rows)

| label | label states | identifier | identity states | recipe rows |
|---|---|---|---|---:|
| `NaH2PO4 x H2O` | 1 | kgmicrobe.compound:nah2po4_x_2_h2o | 2 | 34 |
| `NaH2PO4·H2O` | 1 | kgmicrobe.compound:nah2po4_x_2_h2o | 2 | 1 |
| `NaH2PO4・H2O` | 1 | kgmicrobe.compound:nah2po4_x_2_h2o | 2 | 1 |
| `MgSO4·H2O` | 1 | CHEBI:31795 | 7 (ontology label "magnesium sulfate heptahydrate") | 2 |
| `magnesium sulfate anhydrous` | 0 | CHEBI:31795 | 7 | 0 |
| `Magnesium chloride anhydrous` | 0 | CHEBI:86345 | 6 (ontology label "magnesium dichloride hexahydrate") | 0 |
| `sodium sulfate, anhydrous` | 0 | CHEBI:32586 | 10 | 0 |
| `Anhydrous sodium sulfite` | 0 | CHEBI:86477 | 5 | 0 |
| `Sodium sulfite anhydrous` | 0 | CHEBI:86477 | 5 | 0 |
| `copper(II) nitrate (anhydrous)` | 0 | kgmicrobe.compound:cu_no32_x_3_h2o | 3 | 0 |
| `Cystein-HCl x 2 H2O (5% (w/v))` | 2 | CHEBI:91248 | 1 | 0 |
| `sodium monohydrogen phosphate dihydrat` | 2 | kgmicrobe.ingredient:disodium_phosphate_heptahydrate_~28002_m_stock~29 | 7 | 0 |

The three NaH2PO4 rows are already #758. Rows with 0 recipe rows are latent: they do not affect CultureMech today, but any recipe that uses those spellings would get the wrong hydrate.

## B. One misnamed record: the `MgSO4·H2O` record sits on CHEBI:31795

A MIM record whose preferred term is `MgSO4·H2O` is grounded to CHEBI:31795 (ontology label "magnesium sulfate heptahydrate"). It owns 12 heptahydrate synonyms, so those identities are right and only the record's name contradicts them:
- `MgSO4.7H2O` (23 recipe rows)
- `magnesium sulphate heptahydrate` (1)
- `magnesium sulfate heptahydrate`, `magnesium sulfate (1:1) heptahydrate`, `sulfuric acid magnesium salt heptahydrate`, `.MgSO4 x 7 H2O`, `MgSO x 7 H2O`, `MgSO2 x 7 H2O`, `MgSO4x7H2O`, and three `MgSO4•7H2O (...)` product spellings (0 each)

Either the record is a heptahydrate record with a wrong name, or it is a monohydrate record with a wrong grounding that has collected heptahydrate synonyms. In the second case, the `MgSO4·H2O` label (section A) and these synonyms belong on different records. `build_culturemech_membership.py` already flags this record ("a monohydrate inherits the heptahydrate's memberships").

## Not a defect

`Ceftriaxone disodium salt hemiheptahydrate` → record `Ceftriaxone disodium salt hemi(heptahydrate)` showed up only as a CultureMech parser false positive: the parenthesised prefix is read as "heptahydrate".

## Related

- #811: tombstone cross-hydrate redirects. CultureMech#591 now refuses those on its side; this issue covers the MAPPED cases it cannot.
- #758: NaH2PO4 monohydrate
- #877: membership rebuild




## Resolution (2026-10-15)

- **Fixed:** PR #881 (merged as 3751d80f) handles rows 4-12 and regrounds `MgSO4·H2O` to `cas:14168-73-1`.
- **Rows 1-3 not fixed here:** the NaH2PO4 monohydrate spellings stay with #758.
- **Follow-ups:** #894, #896 and #900-#904.

title: Confirm Sorbitan Monooleate recipe product identity before adding CAS or molecular equivalence
body:
Sorbitan Monooleate now has a usable local material identity, kgmicrobe.ingredient:sorbitan_monooleate, for CultureMech:008837 and CultureMech:008839. Its exact molecular identity remains unresolved.

The primary [ATCC 416 sheet](https://www.atcc.org/-/media/product-assets/documents/microbial-media-formulations/4/1/6/atcc-medium-416.pdf?rev=b4280b8582cc4389a3bdf40c98a7fa03) gives only the generic ingredient name and 1 g/L. The premixed BD product numbers do not identify the scratch ingredient. [JECFA](https://www.fao.org/fileadmin/user_upload/jecfa_additives/docs/Monograph1/Additive-432.pdf) describes a commercial mixture, while CHEBI:183688 depicts a particular molecule. A shared label does not establish exact equivalence.

The inspected KG-Microbe FoodOn source also attaches the bare alias `sorbitan monooleate` and additive numbers 433/494 to CHEBI:53426 (`polysorbate 80`). KG-Microbe's lookup guard contains this route; the upstream annotation needs correction independently.

Closure requires supplier/product or recipe-source evidence for the material, a scoped review of whether CAS 1338-43-8 applies, and review/correction of the FoodOn alias/additive-number conflation. Do not infer Tween 80 or CAS 9005-65-6. Preserve the local identity and both recipe occurrences until then. This evidence hold does not prevent using the reviewed local material record.

Evidence is archived in #754 under `reports/sssom_completion_20260921/mapping_review/`: `chemical-scope-review.md`, `sorbitan-recipe-occurrences.json`, `foodon-sorbitan-conflict.xml` and its source receipt. Related: https://github.com/Knowledge-Graph-Hub/kg-microbe/issues/1123.

title: Two broadMatch rows anchor to a ChEBI term that denotes exactly the substance (step 1 says exactMatch)
body:
Found while measuring the #245 ruling (#735). Two `skos:broadMatch` parent rows point at a ChEBI term that is the substance itself, so Section 3 step 1 applies: `identifier` should be that term with `skos:exactMatch`, and the `cas:` own-identifier row retired per the decision procedure.

| record | identifier now | broadMatch object | why it is exact |
|---|---|---|---|
| `D-Raffinose pentahydrate` (`data/ingredients/mapped/D-Raffinose_Pentahydrate.yaml`) | `cas:17629-30-0` | `CHEBI:189430 Raffinose Pentahydrate`, formula `C18H32O16.5H2O` | same hydrate, same stoichiometry |
| `Sodium succinate dibasic` (`data/ingredients/mapped/Sodium_Succinate_Dibasic.yaml`) | `cas:150-90-3` | `CHEBI:63675 sodium succinate (anhydrous)`, formula `C4H4O4.2Na` | ChEBI's own xref for the term is `cas:150-90-3`; "dibasic" = disodium |

Both records are graded `NARROW_MATCH`. Changing them is an identity change, so it goes through the review bundle (#729–#731), not a hand edit; this issue is the record. Check the remaining 67 molecule-parent broadMatch rows for the same shape before applying (the check is: parent term's CAS xref equals the record's own CAS, or the parent's formula includes the hydrate stoichiometry the label states).

Related: #312, #245.

title: Curator calls surfaced by the #699 review: Na2-citrate on trisodium citrate, Tricine on a grouping class, ledgers that can re-propose retired names
body:
Three findings from reviewers on #699 that need a ruling rather than a rule, filed together because each is small.

**1. `Na2-citrate` is an `EXACT_SYNONYM` on the Trisodium citrate record.** By nomenclature Na2-citrate is *disodium hydrogen* citrate, a different salt from Na3. #699's test cannot see it: that test fires when ChEBI assigns the name to another term, and this ChEBI build has no disodium citrate term at all. The 2026-04-19 `audit_mim_merge` absorbed `Na2-citrate.yaml` *and* `Citric_Acid_2.yaml` / `Citric_Acid_3.yaml` into the trisodium record — so the merge itself conflated an acid and two salts, and summed their occurrence counts. #699 retires `Citric Acid` there; whether recipe rows whose raw label is "Citric Acid" or "Na2-citrate" still count toward this record's 182 occurrences was not checked.

**2. The Tricine record maps to a structureless grouping class.** `Tricine.yaml` → `CHEBI:46760 tricine`, which in this build has a label and nothing else: no formula, no InChIKey, no definition. Its children are `CHEBI:39063` (the neutral form, which owns the structure and the systematic names) and `CHEBI:46759` (the zwitterion). Section 3 asks for the most specific stable identifier; CHEBI:39063 looks like it, and the three tricine names #699 retired from *Lithocholic acid* would be legitimate synonyms there. The record has CAS 5704-04-1 and 44 occurrences.

**3. Two tracked review ledgers still list the cadmium names against calcium nitrate.** `mappings/ingredient_mappings_synonym_enrich_review.tsv` (line 98, `ALREADY_REPRESENTED`) and `mappings/ingredient_mappings_oak_ols_review.tsv` (line 441, verdict `SYNONYM_ENRICH`). They are historical artifacts and probably how the names got in. The backfill is safe — it treats a `REJECTED_LABEL` entry as already present — but a re-run of *that enrichment* reading these ledgers could re-propose them. Either regenerate the ledgers or have the enrichment honour `REJECTED_LABEL`.

Smaller, same records: several carry a stale first `evidence` entry (`DATABASE_MATCH`, "quality=DIRECT_MATCH") that was produced for the original *wrong* mapping and now sits under the corrected `ontology_id`, reading as database support for a mapping it never supported.

title: Sodium glutamate・H2O has a correct record (CHEBI:232425) but resolves to nothing
body:
Found by the #624 rebuild in #653.

Before the rebuild, the surface form `Sodium glutamate・H2O` resolved to `CHEBI:64220` — the **anhydrous** `Na glutamate` record. MAPPING_SEMANTICS §3 refuses that, so the rebuild correctly stops matching it, and the row is now `UNMAPPED`:

```
Sodium glutamate・H2O	4	(chebi_id, cas_rn, kg_microbe_node_id, mim_id all empty)	UNMAPPED
```

But a **correct record already exists**:

```
data/ingredients/mapped/Sodium_Glutamate_Monohydrate.yaml
  identifier: CHEBI:232425
  preferred_term: Sodium glutamate monohydrate
  mapping_status: MAPPED
```

So the substance is curated and the name still goes nowhere — 4 CultureMech occurrences that had a wrong answer now have none.

**Why it misses:** an ignore-inclusive search (`rg -uu`) finds the surface form in no record at all, and the monohydrate record's synonym list carries no hydrate-notation variant:

```
sodium (2S)-2-azaniumylpentanedioate, Glutamate Sodium, Glutamate monosodium salt,
Glutamic acid monosodium salt, Glutammato monosodico, L(+) Sodium glutamate, MSG,
Monosodioglutammato, Natrium L-hydrogenglutamat, Natriumglutaminat,
Sodium hydrogen glutamate, sodium (2S)-2-ammoniopentanedioate
```

Nothing there matches `Sodium glutamate・H2O`, and the separator is U+30FB KATAKANA MIDDLE DOT — the same non-ASCII hydrate notation that shows up elsewhere in this corpus (`(NH4)6Mo7O24・4H2O`).

**Fix:** add the hydrate surface form as a synonym on `Sodium_Glutamate_Monohydrate.yaml` with a `curation_history` event. Worth checking the other `・`-separated forms for the same shape while in there — this is #251's family (hydrate notation hidden in synonyms) seen from the other side.

Not a blocker for #653: the rebuild is a strict improvement over resolving a hydrate to its anhydrous parent.

title: kg-microbe's name index carries 15 recipe instructions as synonyms, which P4.4 will now propose to curators
body:
Found by canarying the revived loader (#578) against the real artifact — the first time this code has ever run on real data.

kg-microbe's unified mapping set indexes a handful of MediaDive recipe annotations as if they were ingredient names. Reviving P4.4 means these become synonym suggestions on MIM records:

```
CHEBI:26710  '(adjust if required in range 100-150)'
CHEBI:26710  '(for Agar medium autoclave separately)'
CHEBI:2509   '(for solid medium)'
CHEBI:2509   '(for solid medium, alternative)'
CHEBI:2511   '(for solid medium, alternative)'
CHEBI:26833  '(sterilized by steaming for 3 hours on 3 consecutive days)'
CHEBI:29377  '(adjust if required)'
CHEBI:32145  '(adjust if required)'
CHEBI:3311   '(if required)'
CHEBI:34545  'NaNO3(autoclave before adding)(Fisher BP360-500)'
CHEBI:17020  'autoclaved, Glucomannan (konjac)'
CHEBI:28087  'autoclaved, Glycogen'
CHEBI:62969  'autoclaved'
CHEBI:62969  'autoclaved, polygalacturonic acid'
CHEBI:201433 'not filter sterilized'
```

**15 forms across 12 entities, out of 369,988 indexed surface forms** — 0.004%. Bounded, and P4.4 suggestions are `auto_correctable=False`, so nothing lands without a curator agreeing. That is why the #578 PR does not add a filter: a hand-written pattern list for fifteen strings is whack-a-mole that will drift, and the real fix belongs upstream where the name index is built.

Catalog codes are the adjacent, larger case and are *not* obviously wrong — `NaCl (Fisher S271-500)` is a real surface form that appears in real recipes, so it should keep being matchable.

Options, roughly in order of preference:

1. Report upstream so the consolidator stops indexing parenthetical instruction fragments as names.
2. If MIM must defend itself, drop surface forms that are wholly parenthesised (`^\(.*\)$`) — that alone catches 8 of the 15 and cannot swallow a legitimate chemical name, which never consists solely of a parenthesised clause.

Not urgent; filed so the noise is on the record before a curator meets it and assumes the check is broken.

title: 9 hydrate labels state a hydration number with no known corresponding hydrate
body:
Found during the adversarial review of #341, by checking each label's stated hydration number against the known stable hydrates of that salt.

| record label | stated n | known hydrates |
|---|---|---|
| `CaCl2 x 7 H2O` | 7 | 1, 2, 4, 6 |
| `CuCl2 x 6 H2O` | 6 | 2 |
| `FeCl2 x 6 H2O` | 6 | 2, 4 |
| `FeCl2 x 7 H2O` | 7 | 2, 4 |
| `FeCl3 x 4 H2O` | 4 | 6 |
| `MgCl2 x 7 H2O` | 7 | 6 |
| `Na2HPO4 x 3 H2O` | 3 | 2, 7, 8, 12 |
| `Na2HPO4 x 6 H2O` | 6 | 2, 7, 8, 12 |
| `NiCl2 x 5 H2O` | 5 | 2, 4, 6 |

10 of the 19 checked do match a known hydrate, so this is not a systematic notation problem — it is 9 specific labels.

## The pattern worth chasing first

`MgCl2 x 7 H2O` and `FeCl2 x 7 H2O` stand out: **`MgSO4·7H2O` and `FeSO4·7H2O` are among the most common salts in microbial growth media**, and both are genuine heptahydrates. A sulfate → chloride slip somewhere upstream would produce exactly these two labels. Worth checking the source rows before assuming the hydration number is what's wrong — it may be the anion.

Note MIM already holds separate `FeSO4 x 7 H2O` records (`CHEBI:75832`/`CHEBI:75836` appear as a same-name-different-identifier pair in the duplicate report), so a comparison against those recipes is possible.

## Relationship to #341

#341 corrected these records' `molecular_formula` from the anhydrous salt's to one that includes the stated water, so for these 9 the formula now faithfully encodes a hydration number that may not correspond to a real substance. That is **not a regression** — the previous value (the anhydrous formula) was wrong for every hydrate — but it does mean the formula is only as good as the label, and these 9 labels are in question.

Resolving this needs the upstream source rows (MediaDive / CultureBotHT / the original recipe text), not chemistry reasoning, so it was filed rather than guessed at.

title: 90 records whose CAS-RN is registered in ChEBI against a different term than their CURIE
body:
## The check

For every record carrying both a `cas_rn` and a CHEBI `ontology_id`, ask which
CHEBI term ChEBI itself registers that CAS against:

```
CAS -> CHEBI index from chebi.db (oio:hasDbXref, 29,736 CAS numbers)

records with CAS + CHEBI id        1370
  CAS registered on THIS term      1074
  CAS not in ChEBI at all           206
  CAS registered on a DIFFERENT term  90   <- defect candidates
```

**This class is invisible to InChIKey comparison**, which is why it survived the
CAS-vs-structure checking done so far: the mis-mapped term is usually a
parent/grouping class with no structure at all, so there is no key to compare.
The failure mode is a name lookup landing on a parent while the CAS points at
the specific child.

## Cross-validation

The check independently rediscovers four defects found separately, one at a time,
by the research lane — before this query existed:

| record | CURIE | CAS points to |
|---|---|---|
| `Ca-pantothenate` | CHEBI:29032 `(R)-pantothenate` | **CHEBI:31345 Calcium pantothenate** (the #315 merge) |
| `02_Thiamine_Pyrophosphate` | CHEBI:9532 | CHEBI:18290 `…diphosphate chloride` |
| `Bicine` | CHEBI:39065 (structureless class) | CHEBI:40957 `N,N-bis(2-hydroxyethyl)glycine` |
| `Aluminium sulfate` | CHEBI:74772 (class) | CHEBI:74768 `aluminium sulfate (anhydrous)` |
| `Bisabolene` | CHEBI:49235 (family class) | CHEBI:49240 `alpha-bisabolene` |

Four separate agents reaching five of these independently, and a mechanical query
reproducing all of them, is good evidence the remaining 85 are real.

## Two sub-classes, different remedies — do not mass-apply

**(a) CURIE is a parent; the label names the specific child.** Fix the CURIE.
`Bicine` (a structureless grouping class with a disjunctive definition),
`Bisabolene` (family over 16 terms — note `C15H24` is shared by all of them, so
a formula check passes on the wrong term), `Ca-pantothenate`, `Aluminium sulfate`,
`alpha-Lactose` → `Alpha-lactose monohydrate`, `Carboxymethyl cellulose` →
`carboxymethylcellulose sodium`.

**(b) CURIE is correctly generic for a generic label; the *CAS* is over-specific.**
Fix or drop the CAS, not the mapping. `Arginine` (CHEBI:29016, stereo-agnostic —
correct for a bare label) whose CAS 74-79-3 is L-arginine's; `Ascorbic acid`
(CHEBI:22652) with L-ascorbic acid's CAS; `D-Ribose` with D-ribofuranose's.

Sub-class (b) is the same shape as the bare-anion convention in #319: a
deliberately generic term is right for a generic label, and it is the
*over-specific companion field* that is wrong. Getting this backwards would
break correct records.

## Suggested action

Triage the 90 into (a) and (b); the discriminator is whether the record's own
label is generic or specific. Then add the query as a standing check — it is
cheap, needs only `chebi.db`, and catches a class nothing else does.

Also worth noting the 206 "CAS not in ChEBI at all": not a defect by itself, but
it is the population where a wrong CAS can hide indefinitely, since neither this
check nor an InChIKey comparison can adjudicate it.

## Provenance

Proposed by the Claude research lane after it hit the same shape three times
(`Bicine`, `Bisabolene`, `02_Thiamine_Pyrophosphate`) and observed that InChIKey
comparison structurally cannot catch it. Verified repo-wide against chebi.db.
Related: #315, #316, #317, #319.

title: Salt-named records mapped EXACT_MATCH to the bare anion (10 records)
body:
## Finding

Ten records whose **label explicitly names a counterion or says "salt"** carry a
mapping whose **recorded structure is a net-charged ion**. Seven are graded
`EXACT_MATCH` — the strongest identity claim available, asserting that a salt
*is* its anion.

| net charge | identifier | quality | label | term (verified OLS4) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| −2 | CHEBI:16810 | **EXACT_MATCH** | `Na2 alpha-ketoglutarate` | `2-oxoglutarate(2-)` |
| −2 | CHEBI:29988 | **EXACT_MATCH** | `Na-glutamate` | `L-glutamate(2-)` |
| −2 | CHEBI:30924 | **EXACT_MATCH** | `Na-tartrate` | `L-tartrate(2-)` |
| −1 | CHEBI:29032 | **EXACT_MATCH** | `Ca-pantothenate` | `(R)-pantothenate` |
| −1 | CHEBI:35899 | **EXACT_MATCH** | `Na-crotonate` | `crotonate` |
| +1 | CHEBI:46020 | **EXACT_MATCH** | `Tetramethyl ammonium` | (cation) |
| −2 | cas:12208-13-8 | FALLBACK_REGISTRY | `potassium hexahydroxoantimonate` | — |
| −1 | cas:207511-06-6 | NARROW_MATCH | `L-Malic acid disodium salt monohydrate` | — |
| +1 | cas:9067-32-7 | NARROW_MATCH | `Hyaluronic acid sodium salt from S. equi` | — |
| +1 | kgmicrobe.compound:… | CLOSE_MATCH | `Tetramethyl ammonium chloride` | — |

All five CHEBI labels above verified live against OLS4; none obsolete.

## Why these are not covered by the #213 convention

MIM deliberately grounds **bare anion labels** (`Fumarate`, `Citrate`, `Lactate`)
to the fully-deprotonated CHEBI class, and that is correct — a bare label carries
no counterion, and the anion is the species present at growth-medium pH.

These ten are a different case: the label **names the counterion**
(`Na2 …`, `Ca-…`, `… sodium salt`). Sodium glutamate and glutamate(2−) are
different substances with different formulas, masses and CAS numbers. So the
convention does not license `EXACT_MATCH` here, and the anion mapping — while a
reasonable *close/narrow* relation — overstates as identity.

Note also `Na-glutamate`: monosodium glutamate is the **mono**-anion salt, so
even the charge state of the current target is off by one.

## Detection

Mechanical and high-precision. Net charge must be computed across **both** InChI
layers — `/q` alone gives 119 false positives, because a neutral salt like AlCl3
is written `/q+3;;;/p-3`:

```python
net = sum(component /q charges) + /p          # non-zero  => recorded structure is an ion
defect = net != 0 and label names a counterion or "salt"
```

That narrows 119 → 40 → **10**, with no false positives in the 10 on inspection.

## Suggested action

Per record: either re-ground to a CHEBI salt term where one exists, or keep the
anion term and downgrade `mapping_quality` to `CLOSE_MATCH`/`NARROW_MATCH` with
the reason recorded. The `EXACT_MATCH` grade is the part that is indefensible.

Worth adding the check to the validation suite so a future promotion sweep
cannot reintroduce it.

## Provenance

Surfaced by the Claude research lane on `1-ethyl-3-methylimidazolium_Lysine`
(CHEBI:61326 is the [C2mim]⁺ cation alone; the ingredient is a neutral salt),
then generalised repo-wide. Related: #312 (ledger triage), #309 (the two-lane
harness).

title: Does the Section 3 narrowMatch pattern extend to source-material records?
body:
The Edison literature sweep surfaced two records whose reports identify a
confident ontology term while explicitly refusing to assert an identity mapping:

| record | term | report's words |
|---|---|---|
| `Calf brains` | `UBERON:0000955` *brain* | "high-confidence anatomical-source annotation" but "do **not** assert `skos:exactMatch` or `skos:closeMatch`" |
| `Cow manure` | `ENVO:00003031` *animal manure* | recommends retaining UNMAPPED |

Both terms resolve correctly against the local builds, and both prefixes are
already in `promote_resolved_unmapped.py`'s `ONTOLOGY_DB`.

The reports forbid `exactMatch` and `closeMatch` — the two predicates that
license node substitution. They do not mention `skos:narrowMatch`, which is
exactly the predicate that says the subject is *narrower than* the object
without claiming they are interchangeable, and which MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md
Section 3 already uses for hydrates (`NaH2PO4*H2O` narrowMatch the anhydrous
`CHEBI:37585`).

So the question is a policy one, not a lookup one: **is Section 3's
identifier + narrowMatch + Rule B1 registry row pattern meant only for
hydrate/salt variants of a parent compound, or does it also cover
source-qualified materials** — calf brains as a narrower thing than brain, cow
manure than animal manure, larchwood xylan than xylan?

Arguments each way:

- **For extending it.** These records would gain a real, correct, non-substituting
  edge into UBERON/ENVO, which is more than the current UNMAPPED conveys. The
  narrowMatch semantics are literally true.
- **Against.** "Calf brains" as a medium ingredient is a *preparation*, and
  narrowMatch on a preparation-to-anatomy axis is a different relation from
  narrowMatch on a hydrate-to-anhydrous axis. Conflating them makes the
  predicate mean two things, and kg-microbe consumers cannot tell which.
  UBERON:0000955 as an *anatomical source* — which is what the report actually
  recommends — is arguably a schema slot, not an SSSOM row.

Nothing was applied; the records stay UNMAPPED and the CURIEs are recorded in
their curation history. Raising this because the same question governs a
recurring class of records (extracts, tissue preparations, source-qualified
polymers), and deciding it once is better than deciding it per record.

Blocked on a curator's call; see also #236 on subject/file identity.

title: 87 published labels resolve to more than one identifier, including 18 preferred_term-vs-synonym collisions
body:
Found reviewing #231, which introduces the ambiguity by publishing synonyms.

Before #231, `docs/data/*.csv` carried only `preferred_term`, and **preferred_terms are unique** (verified: zero duplicates). So the CSV supported an unambiguous `{label: identifier}` join. Publishing synonyms makes that join order-dependent for **87 labels**.

The sharp cases are where **one record's `preferred_term` is another record's synonym** — a consumer's answer depends purely on row order:

| label | holders |
|---|---|
| `Vitamin B12` | CHEBI:176843 (preferred) / CHEBI:17439 (synonym) / UNMAPPED_0005 (synonym) |
| `Mannitol` | CHEBI:29864 (preferred) / CHEBI:16899 (synonym) |
| `Tryptophan` | CHEBI:27897 (preferred) / CHEBI:16828 (synonym) |
| `Citrate` | CHEBI:16947 (preferred) / CHEBI:30769 (synonym) |
| `Sulfur` | CHEBI:26833 (preferred) / CHEBI:17909 (synonym) |
| `Putrescine` | CHEBI:17148 (preferred) / cas:333-93-7 (synonym) |

…and ~12 more of that shape.

Some of these are the #218 family in another guise — `Citrate`/`Citric acid`, `Sulfur`, `Mannitol` are the same substance under two CHEBI ids, i.e. the inverse defect of #225. Others are legitimately shared synonyms where two distinct terms both accept a loose common name.

#231 does **not** treat this as a failure — a synonym legitimately can be shared, and failing the build on it would block the fix. The gate prints it as a note.

## What to decide

1. Which of the 87 are the #225/#218 inverse defect (one substance, two ids) and should be merged, versus genuinely-shared loose names.
2. For the genuine ones, whether the published surface should carry a precedence signal so a consumer can resolve deterministically — e.g. a `match_type` column distinguishing preferred_term from synonym, so `Vitamin B12` → CHEBI:176843 is the documented answer.

Until (2), consumers joining on the `synonyms` column should prefer a row whose `preferred_term` equals the query.

Related: #231, #229, #218, #225.
